name: Lupus
introduction: is the Wolf, a wild animal that the Greeks and Romans pictured impaled on a spear held by the Centaur. It lies in the southern Milky Way between Centaurus and Scorpius.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Lupus is filled with hot blue stars belonging to the Scorpius–Centaurus association, the nearest large family of young massive stars, about 400 to 500 light-years away. Dark [Lupus clouds](id:cahlon-cloud-31) are still giving birth to new, Sun-like stars.

In the year 1006, the brightest supernova in recorded history appeared in Lupus. Astronomers in China, Egypt, Iraq, Japan and Europe described a star bright enough to cast shadows and visible in daylight for weeks.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Uridim](hip:71860), [Beta Lupi](hip:73273), [Gamma Lupi](hip:76297) and [Delta Lupi](hip:75141) are all hot blue giants and subgiants of the Scorpius–Centaurus family.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The remnant of SN 1006 still glows in X-rays and radio waves. Lupus also contains the globular cluster NGC 5986 and the Retina Nebula, a planetary nebula seen edge-on.
